notes: Event date: 22 April 1945 (CMH The Last Offensive, p. 429). Event definition: After crossing the interarmy boundary to Tuebingen (18 April) and enveloping the city by Esslingen (21 April), the army clears Stuttgart on 22 April, taking some 28,000 prisoners in twelve days. Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). CMH The Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 429: "a French column the next day pushed down the valley of the Neckar by way of Esslingen, enveloped Stuttgart, and broke into the northeastern fringe of the city early in the afternoon"; "The following day, 22 April, Stuttgart was clear"; "de Lattre's First French Army in twelve days had swept the northern half of the Black Forest, trapped the bulk of the LXIV Corps, and seized Stuttgart". Location: Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg with a precision of 25 km. Location support: the source names Stuttgart and the date; precision 25 km for an army. Commander: General Jean de Lattre de Tassigny commands Army B, later the First French Army (CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 27; Wikipedia).
